mde.formula: e80 = s80 x sigma_h / sqrt(n): P7.2 'Per trade (random-walk sigma_h; independent trades every date): 0.71 ticks net at 5-minute holds and 4 trades a date ...' (p7_final 'mu at selection threshold' = threshold x sigma_h / sqrt(n), sigma_h = 3.15 sqrt(h)), with the threshold replaced by s80 = bar + z_0.80 se(bar), se = sqrt((1 + bar^2/2)/(T_disc - 1)) (p7_final's s80 convention, its test line '80% power needs a true daily Sharpe of 0.1936'), T_disc = 796

multiple_comparisons.reading: P07: p = 1 - Phi(daily t), no t -> p = 1 counted in m; BH q 0.05; Holm 0.05

alternatives_not_used.reason: pooling the 400 values as iid draws (mean m, SD s) mixes the configurations' different null means into the spread; its n = 20 prediction misses the observed per-seed maxima by far, so it is not used

expected_max_report.method: REPORT, not a gate. The null's per-configuration spread is P4.2's statistic: the SD of the 400 null daily Sharpes, each centred on its configuration's mean over the 20 seeds (sigma_c, population; df-corrected x sqrt(20/19)). Zero-edge null for the 300: every configuration's true daily Sharpe 0, independent sampling errors with SD sigma_c; E[max over n] = expected_max_sharpe(n, sigma_c^2) (Bailey and Lopez de Prado 2014 eq. 3, the program's function; the same construction as SR0, which uses 1/sqrt(T_disc - 1) in place of sigma_c). Check of the construction at n = 20 in B5's own setting: E[max_c (mu_c + sigma_c,df eps_c)] by Monte Carlo (100,000 draws, seed 20261028; mu_c = each null configuration's mean over the seeds) against the mean of the 20 observed per-seed maxima. Caveats: independence overstates the max for correlated configurations; true Sharpes of a real null search are below 0 by costs (the B5 null mean is negative), which lowers the max; the null covers S5 x {F15, T30} only.
